newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures edge higher in day of uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures edge higher in day of uncertainty.

text.p: German debt recovered from early losses to trade slightly higher late in the day Monday as dealers covered short-positions taken ahead of French elections over the weekend.
The DTB June Bund future contract was six basis points higher at 100.75 after having traded in a range between 100.43 and 100.91.

Traders said that although socialists prevailed at the polls in France, the market did not fall as far as had been expected and European debt traders opted to cover speculative positions taken ahead of the election.
"Nervousness is the greatest poison in this market," one trader said.
Indeed, the Bonn-Bundesbank gold revaluation saga continued to undermine confidence in monetary union.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel held out the possability of a compromise with the central bank while several members of the council continued to say the revaluation scheme as it now stands would hurt confidence in the euro.
Traders said worries about how the rare fight between Bonn and the Bundesbank will play out promise to limit the market's upside at around 101.00 in the near term.
Traders said there was a lot of speculation of switching out of German debt and into Treasuries but that little of this seemed to have actually taken place.
Germany's manufacturing sector expanded at an accelerated pace in May as more bottlenecks emerged, driving up prices, according to the BME/Reuters German Purchasing Managers Index.
The index, first published last month, rose to a seasonally-adjusted 57.49 in May from 56.58 in April.
Traders said that given nervousness in the market, the futures contract should trade roughly between 100.40 and 101.00 over the next couple of days.
The benchmark 10-year cash Bund climbed to 100.51 from 100.43 to yield 5.925 percent.
The T-note/Bund gap, meanwhile, climbed out slightly on the day to 86 basis points.
